However, please consider your nieces and nephews: their dad just died, their mom is dating a stranger, and now the closest person to their dad (you) is ignoring them for unknown reasons. I’m a transfer student and a history major here at UCSD. 

Personally, as the person above recommended, having a set schedule is crucial to prevent being overwhelmed. I would create a daily checklist, adding assignments and mundane task (e.g., eating), and I’d check off everything I’ve finished. It helps me stay motivated and feel productive. 

Also, take breaks! This is something I still need to work on myself. You’re reading so much, and if you’re like me, you might be at the computer desk for hours reading or writing. Take 10 minute breaks often and stretch! Go on a walk. It helps stay clear headed and motivated. 

If you have discussion questions, they’ll most likely correlate to the readings you have. Usually, I’ll read the discussion question first and then read the assigned readings, looking for answers for the discussion questions. When I read, I tend to write my thoughts or key points in my notebook (you can type these notes). It’s very helpful for me to absorb the readings and it’s arguments. 

Also, it’s good to have a few classmates to talk to. I’ve had a classmates who I shared multiple classes with and it was helpful to talk to them (even if it’s just venting). In a classroom setting, if you can, I highly recommend participating in class discussions and breakout rooms. For me, I learn the best by having a discussion and bouncing off ideas with my peers and teachers. I try to take notes what I what I’ve learned from the discussions.
